questions.q: Why does Northbridge run northbridge-aks-dev and northbridge-aks-prod as two separate clusters instead of one?
options: AKS does not support multiple namespaces on one cluster
Terraform cannot create two clusters from the same module
Isolating prod means a noisy or misbehaving dev workload can never starve prod of node capacity
Azure requires a separate cluster per region
questions.explain: northbridge-aks-dev hosts both dev and staging namespaces to save cost; northbridge-aks-prod is fully isolated so production workloads never compete with dev/staging for the same nodes.

questions.q: What VM size and autoscaling range do Northbridge's AKS node pools use?
options: Standard_D4s_v5, autoscaling 2 to 5 nodes
Standard_B2s, a fixed 3 nodes
Standard_D4s_v5, autoscaling 10 to 20 nodes
Standard_F8s, no autoscaling
questions.explain: Both the system and user node pools in the azurerm_kubernetes_cluster resource use Standard_D4s_v5 with autoscaling bounded between 2 and 5 nodes.

questions.q: Why does Northbridge split workloads across a system node pool and a separate user node pool?
options: User pools are cheaper per vCPU than system pools
So application traffic spikes (e.g. a flash sale hitting checkout) scale the user pool without risking the nodes cluster infrastructure like CoreDNS depends on
System pools cannot run on Standard_D4s_v5 VMs
Kubernetes requires at least two node pools to schedule any pod
questions.explain: The system pool runs cluster components like CoreDNS and the ingress controller; the user pool runs product-catalog and checkout, so scaling under load never touches the nodes the cluster itself relies on.

questions.q: How does northbridgeacr.azurecr.io let AKS pull images without a stored imagePullSecret?
options: The registry is public and requires no authentication at all
Each pod manifest embeds a base64-encoded password
An azurerm_role_assignment grants the cluster's kubelet identity the AcrPull role, scoped to the registry
ACR automatically trusts any AKS cluster in the same Azure tenant
questions.explain: The kubelet identity (the node's managed identity) is granted the built-in AcrPull role on the ACR resource via a Terraform role assignment, so nodes authenticate without any stored credential.

questions.q: Which components typically run in the system node pool rather than the user node pool?
options: The checkout and product-catalog application pods
CoreDNS, metrics-server, and the ingress controller's control-plane pods
The PaymentPro payment processor
The Terraform state blob
questions.explain: The system node pool hosts cluster infrastructure components; application workloads like checkout and product-catalog run on the user node pool instead.
